_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: a mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so `s.stdio.semio.cad`'s (non-)oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `s.stdio.semio.cad` is a semio-NATIVE format — no third party in any ecosystem reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` — so no oracle is registered (see noOracleDecisions below).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over this subset's `SemioCadMutation` vocabulary — that vocabulary IS this subset's own specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute. The nearest candidate was surveyed and rejected on the merits rather than for absence: this subset ships real DXF R12 / STEP AP214 / DWG AC1024 import and export serializers under `../🚪️io/`, and `dxf` 0.6 and `ruststep` 0.4 are BOTH already linked into this owner's oracle crate, so a `dxf`-mediated differential looks available. It is not: the oracle role must produce its reference answer from the committed input alone and must never link the subject crate, so the only way to hand `dxf` a drawing would be to route the semio snapshot through THIS repository's own DXF exporter first — which makes the reference an artefact of the implementation it is supposed to judge. Worse, the R12 profile cannot express the vocabulary being measured: `add-block-entity`/`remove-block-entity`/`set-block-entity-layer`/`set-block-entity-geometry` address an entity INSIDE a block definition by handle, and DXF's `BLOCKS` section has no per-entity handle addressing that survives a write-read cycle, so four of these sixteen kinds would have had nothing to compare against and would silently degrade into comparing our output with our own output — the one failure this platform exists to prevent. The cross-language hosts have landed — the runner materializes a Rust, a Python (cache-local interpreter), a TypeScript (npm-resolving), a Go and a .NET host — so a Python or JavaScript reference was checked as well, and it fails one level earlier than a Rust one would: no package in any of those registries reads a semio envelope at all, because the `semio <envelope-id> v1` preamble, the hex/bracket value grammar and the LEB128 pack framing are defined by this repository alone. Confidence comes instead from specification vectors — the committed `(before, mutation, after)` triple per kind under this case's own `🧫️fixtures/`, derived by an INDEPENDENT Python implementation of both the committed DSL grammar and this vocabulary's specification (`.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR/🐍️semio-pattern-a-vectors.py`), never by running this repository's own Rust — plus the metamorphic inverse law: applying a mutation and then its own computed inverse must restore the pre-mutation snapshot exactly. The `identity-round-trip` scenario ties the two together by asserting that production's own `parse_dsl` of the SAME real artifact equals the `before` snapshot every vector starts from, so a mistake in the Python decoder surfaces as a red scenario rather than as a quietly agreeable one.
